newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico drug king owned restaurant where six died.
newsitem.headline: Mexico drug king owned restaurant where six died.

text.p: Amado Carrillo Fuentes, the Mexican cocaine baron whose death has sparked a bloody turf war among drug traffickers, owned the border restaurant where six people were killed this week, a U.S. anti-narcotics official said on Wednesday.

The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said Carrillo owned the fashionable Maxfim resaurant in Ciudad Juarez where the drug hit happened on Sunday night, and that the attack was clearly linked to a bitter struggle for control of the multi-billion dollar cocaine trade.
"Of course it's related to the Carrillo Fuentes drug wars," the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration official said.

Two well-dressed men marched into Maxfim on Sunday night and sprayed 150 rounds from AK-47 assault rifles at a group of people seated at a table before fleeing in a black Jaguar. Six people were killed in the attack and three more were wounded.
It was the worst incident in an escalating drug war touched off when Carrillo Fuentes died after having plastic surgery in Mexico City on July 4.

The main target of the attack was Alfonso Corral Olaguez, 36, also known as "Green Feet" because he always wore green, crocodile-skin cowboy boots. Mexican police said Corral Olaguez was an informant for the DEA and was apparently a nephew of Jaime Herrera, the leader of a cartel operating in the Mexican state of Durango.
The assailants shot Corral 25 times with an AK-47 and then again at point blank range in the back of the head with a .45 calibre pistol. His two bodyguards were also killed.
The DEA official said the Herrera and Carrillo cartels compete but "get along and know how to work together" so he doubted they were now at war with each other.
Since Carrillo's death, some 20 people have been killed in drug-related incidents in Ciudad Juarez, which lies just across the border from El Paso, Texas.
